categories.main_business_segments: The Miyazaki Bank Group operates primarily in three business segments: banking (including deposits, loans, domestic and foreign exchange, and related services), leasing (through its subsidiary Miyagin Lease Co., Ltd.), and other financial services such as credit guarantees, venture capital, and credit card operations via its subsidiaries.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The bank relies on advanced digital banking systems, integrated online platforms, and robust risk management frameworks. It employs both traditional face-to-face banking and digital/non-face-to-face channels, with ongoing investments in digital transformation (DX), cybersecurity, and operational efficiency through IT and automation.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are individuals and businesses in Miyazaki Prefecture and surrounding regions, including SMEs, local governments, and public institutions. The bank also serves retail clients with personal loans, mortgages, and asset management products, as well as corporate clients with financing, leasing, and consulting services.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are concentrated in Miyazaki Prefecture, with a network of 70 branches and offices, and additional presence in neighboring prefectures (Kagoshima, Oita, Kumamoto, Fukuoka) and Tokyo. The vast majority of business is domestic, with over 90% of revenue and assets located in Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: The Miyazaki Bank operates as a downstream financial services provider, directly serving end customers (individuals, businesses, and public entities) with banking, leasing, and related financial products. It does not function as an intermediary or upstream supplier in the financial value chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include digital transformation (DX), enhancing both physical and digital customer touchpoints, strengthening consulting and solution capabilities, and supporting regional sustainability and ESG initiatives. The bank is focused on integrating real and digital channels, expanding non-face-to-face services, and investing in human capital and reskilling.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated from interest income on loans and securities, service fees (including asset management, settlement, and consulting), leasing income, and credit guarantee and card fees. The bank also earns from investment activities and commissions on insurance and investment products.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include other regional banks, national megabanks expanding into the region, and non-bank financial institutions. Miyazaki Bank positions itself as a leading regional bank with deep local roots and a strong focus on community-based, sustainable growth, aiming to be the 'First Call Bank' for local stakeholders.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of March 2025, the bank had total assets of approximately ¥4.07 trillion, deposits of ¥3.16 trillion, and loans outstanding of ¥2.39 trillion. FY2024 consolidated ordinary income was ¥80.2 billion, with net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥9.78 billion, showing a growth trajectory in both revenue and profit over the past year.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The bank emphasizes its role as an indispensable regional financial infrastructure, combining personalized, face-to-face service with advanced digital solutions. Its differentiation lies in deep local engagement, comprehensive financial solutions tailored to regional needs, and a strong commitment to sustainability, ESG, and supporting the long-term growth of the local community.
